Questions, answered

Clarity from the start.

Is MyIFA my financial adviser?

No. MyIFA is an independent consumer services company providing tools, information and a provider pathway. Personal financial advice and product solutions are provided by independent providers under their own authorisation and agreements.

Am I obliged to buy something or meet an adviser?

No. You can use the available tools and read the information without accepting an introduction or purchasing a product. Any future advice or product fees must be disclosed and agreed with the relevant provider.

Are the tools and personal report free to use?

The tools in this website version are available without payment or an account. They produce educational estimates rather than financial advice. Provider services may carry fees, which must be disclosed separately before you agree to them.

Does MyIFA share my toolkit answers?

This version does not send toolkit answers to MyIFA or any adviser. Optional progress saving uses this browser’s local storage. You choose whether to print or download your report, and who to share it with.

Can I choose my own provider through MyIFA?

No. Provider selection is an internal MyIFA process. Tell us your needs and MyIFA chooses the provider to introduce. You remain free to accept or decline the introduction and are under no obligation to buy a product.

How are providers selected?

MyIFA chooses providers for clients through an internal process. Clients describe their needs but do not browse a directory, compare providers or make the provider selection themselves. MyIFA’s intended criteria include relevant authorisation, service scope, independence and commercial disclosures. You decide whether to proceed with the provider MyIFA selects. Introductions are not active in this preview and no providers have been listed as accredited.

Do I need to supply FICA documents to browse?

No. Browsing and using these tools do not require identity documents. A relevant accountable institution may require identity verification and other due-diligence information if you later enter an advisory or product relationship. That provider explains its requirements.
